topics: 💧 Blessing on Water — Rabbi Tarfon's 'Who creates many forms of life'; 'go out and see what the people do'
🤝 Zimmun Begins — the mishna: three who ate together must join; who counts toward the three and who does not
📖 The Source of Zimmun — 'Praise God with me' (Psalms 34:4) and 'give praise to our God' (Deut. 32:3)
🔊 Not Louder Than the Leader — one answering amen, and the translator beside the Torah reader
✌️ Two Who Ate Together — may they form an optional zimmun? Rav vs. Rabbi Yoḥanan and four failed proofs
🏃 The Diner Who Left — calling him from the market; three vs. ten; halakha like Mar Zutra
🙏 Responding to a Zimmun — 'barukh u'mevorakh' vs. amen; amen after one's own 'Who builds Jerusalem'

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Three Who Ate as One
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 45a–45b
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: After closing the previous chapter with the blessing over water — where the Gemara's ruling is simply 'go out and see what the people do' — the daf opens the chapter on zimmun. The mishna lays out who joins the three: eaters of doubtfully tithed produce, redeemed tithes, a waiter who ate an olive-bulk, and a Samaritan count; eaters of untithed produce, a gentile, women, slaves and minors do not. The Gemara finds the source in Psalms and Deuteronomy, adds that a respondent's amen and a translator's voice must not overpower the leader, and then argues at length whether two who ate together may form a zimmun voluntarily. It closes with the practicalities: the diner who stepped out, the one who interrupts his meal for the others, three equal Sages who lost their zimmun by blessing separately, and what a latecomer answers when he finds the group already blessing.

slides.title: 🤝 Who Counts Toward a Zimmun of Three?
slides.subtitle: The mishna's two lists, and the minimum amount eaten
rows: Ate first tithe whose teruma was separated
Ate first tithe whose teruma was not separated
Ate second tithe or consecrated food that was redeemed
Ate second tithe or consecrated food not redeemed
The waiter who ate an olive-bulk
The waiter who ate less than an olive-bulk
Minimum: an olive-bulk (כְּזַיִת); Rabbi Yehuda: an egg-bulk (כְּבֵיצָה)
Women, slaves, and minors do not obligate those they ate with

callout.label: Before the chapter began:
callout.text: The mishna's Rabbi Tarfon says the blessing over water is 'Who creates many forms of life and their needs'. Asked which opinion is the halakha, Abaye (or Rav Yosef) answered: פּוֹק חֲזִי מַאי עַמָּא דָּבַר — go out and see what the people do. And one who drank water only because a piece of meat choked him recites no blessing at all.

slides.title: 📖 Where Does Zimmun Come From — and Why Not Shout Amen?
slides.subtitle: Two verses for the mitzva, and two lessons about the volume of a response
slides.hebrewSource: גַּדְּלוּ לַה׳ אִתִּי וּנְרוֹמְמָה שְׁמוֹ יַחְדָּו
slides.label: The sources:
slides.text: Rav Asi derives zimmun from 'Praise God with me, and we will exalt His name together' (Psalms 34:4): the leader turns to at least two others. Rabbi Abbahu derives it from 'When I call the Name of the Lord, give [plural] praise to our God' (Deuteronomy 32:3). From the word 'together' Rav Ḥanan bar Abba adds that one who answers amen should not raise his voice above the one blessing. Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi learns the same for the translator of the public Torah reading: 'Moses spoke, and God responded in a voice' (Exodus 19:19) — 'in a voice' is superfluous unless it means in Moses' voice, no louder. A baraita adds the reverse: if the translator cannot match the reader, the reader lowers his voice.

callout.label: Principle:
callout.text: Zimmun is collective praise — 'together' means matched, not competing, voices.

slides.title: ✌️ Can Two Who Ate Together Choose to Form a Zimmun?
slides.subtitle: Rav and Rabbi Yoḥanan disagree; the Gemara tests four proofs and identifies who said what

lines.speaker: Proof 1
lines.text: Mishna: three who ate as one must form a zimmun — three yes, two no!

lines.speaker: Reply
lines.text: There the mishna speaks of an obligatory zimmun; our dispute is about an optional one.

lines.speaker: Proof 2
lines.text: Baraita: three may not disperse. If two could form a zimmun, why forbid one of the three from leaving?

lines.speaker: Reply
lines.text: Different — from the outset they were established as an obligatory three and may not trade it for an option. The same answers the waiter who may join two uninvited but not three, and Rav's rule about calling back a diner who left.

lines.speaker: Proof 3
lines.text: Baraita: women form a zimmun among themselves, though a hundred women are like two men for a quorum. So two men may too!

lines.speaker: Reply
lines.text: Different — there are three separate minds (דֵּעוֹת). And women and slaves may not join together only because of concern for promiscuity.

lines.speaker: Conclusion
lines.text: It is Rabbi Yoḥanan who forbids: he taught that of two who ate together, one fulfils his duty through the other's blessing — and Rabbi Zeira explained this teaches there is no zimmun blessing between them. The Western Sages who permit heard it from Rav before he descended to Babylonia (Rav Huna).

callout.label: Abaye's tradition:
callout.text: Two who ate together — it is a mitzva to separate and each bless for himself. A baraita agrees, but only when both are learned; if one is learned and one an ignoramus, the learned one blesses and the other fulfils his obligation.

slides.title: 🏃 One Stepped Out, One Still Eating, Three Who Blessed Alone
slides.subtitle: Practical rulings on holding a zimmun together

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rav (via Rav Dimi bar Yosef): three ate together and one went out to the market — they call him and include him in the zimmun
2️⃣ Abaye: only if they call and he answers
3️⃣ Mar Zutra: that suffices for three; for ten they wait until he comes and sits
4️⃣ Rav Ashi objects: the opposite is logical — nine look like ten, but two do not look like three
5️⃣ Halakha follows Mar Zutra: with ten, God's Name is invoked, and it is not proper conduct to do so with fewer than ten present
6️⃣ Rava (and Rabbi Zeira): one interrupts his meal to join the two, but two do not interrupt for one — Rav Pappa did so for his son Abba Mar only beyond the letter of the law

7️⃣ Yehuda bar Mareimar, Mar bar Rav Ashi and Rav Aḥa of Difti, none greater than the other, each blessed alone. Mareimar: you fulfilled Grace but not zimmun — and אֵין זִימּוּן לְמַפְרֵעַ, there is no retroactive zimmun

slides.title: 🙏 What Does a Latecomer Answer — and Amen After Your Own Blessing?
slides.subtitle: Rav Zevid and Rav Pappa do not really disagree; two baraitot are reconciled

boxes.title: Found them saying 'Nevarekh'
items: He answers בָּרוּךְ וּמְבוֹרָךְ — 'Blessed is He and blessed is His Name' (Rav Zevid)

boxes.title: Amen after one's own blessing
items: Resolution: praiseworthy after Who builds Jerusalem; reprehensible in other blessings
Abaye answered it aloud so his workers would hear and rise to work, since 'Who is good and does good' is not Torah law
Rav Ashi answered it in a whisper so that people would not belittle 'Who is good and does good'

callout.label: Pattern:
callout.text: The same move resolves both questions: two rulings that look contradictory are each speaking about a different moment in the blessing.

summary.principle: Zimmun is collective praise — 'Praise God with me' needs three minds, obligates them once they sat down together, and cannot be recovered once they blessed apart.

flowSteps.content: 🤝 Mishna: three who ate as one must form a zimmun; demai-eater, waiter with an olive-bulk, Kuti count; tevel-eater, gentile, women/slaves/minors do not
📖 Source: 'Praise God with me… together' (Ps. 34:4) / 'give praise to our God' (Deut. 32:3) → amen and the translator not louder than the leader
❓ Two who ate: optional zimmun? Every proof is deflected (obligation vs. option; three minds). Conclusion: Rabbi Yoḥanan forbids — one fulfils his duty through the other, no zimmun between them

columns.content: 🏃 One who left: call him and he answers (three); must be present for ten — halakha like Mar Zutra
✋ One interrupts for two, not two for one; no retroactive zimmun (Mareimar)

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: Match the response to the moment — 'barukh u'mevorakh' at 'nevarekh', amen at 'barukh', and amen after one's own 'Who builds Jerusalem' only

quiz.q: Which of the following diners counts toward the three needed for zimmun according to the mishna?
o: A waiter who ate less than an olive-bulk
One who ate untithed produce (tevel)
A Samaritan (Kuti) who ate with two Jews
A gentile who ate with two Jews
quiz.e: The mishna lists the Kuti among those who count, alongside a waiter who ate an olive-bulk and eaters of demai and redeemed tithes. A gentile, a tevel-eater, and a waiter who ate less than an olive-bulk do not count.

quiz.q: What does Rav Ḥanan bar Abba derive from 'Praise God with me, and we will exalt His name together'?
o: That zimmun requires ten people
That one answering amen should not raise his voice louder than the one blessing
That women may not form a zimmun
That the translator must speak louder than the reader
quiz.e: The word 'together' teaches that the response should match, not exceed, the leader's voice. Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi derives the parallel rule for the translator from 'God responded in a voice' — in Moses' voice.

quiz.q: How does the Gemara answer the proof from the baraita that women form a zimmun for themselves, even though a hundred women are like two men for a quorum?
o: Women are exempt from zimmun entirely
There are three separate minds among three women, which two men lack
The baraita follows Rav, not Rabbi Yoḥanan
Women may only form a zimmun with slaves
quiz.e: The Gemara says 'there it is different because there are minds' (דֵּעוֹת) — three individuals can fulfil 'praise God with me… together', while two men cannot. Women and slaves may not combine only because of concern for promiscuity.

quiz.q: Why is the halakha in accordance with Mar Zutra that for a zimmun of ten the absent diner must actually return?
o: Because nine do not look like ten
Because a zimmun of ten invokes the Name of Heaven, and it is not proper conduct to do so with fewer than ten present
Because Rav Ashi agreed with him
Because the absent diner cannot hear from the market
quiz.e: Rav Ashi argued the opposite was more logical (nine look like ten, two do not look like three), but the Gemara rules like Mar Zutra because mentioning God's Name with fewer than ten present is not proper.

quiz.q: One arrives and finds the group saying 'Nevarekh'. What does he answer, and what did Mareimar tell the three Sages who each blessed alone?
o: Amen; they should form a zimmun now
'Barukh u'mevorakh'; they fulfilled Grace but not zimmun, and there is no retroactive zimmun
'Barukh u'mevorakh'; they must recite Grace again
Nothing; two of them may still form a zimmun
quiz.e: Rav Zevid: at 'Nevarekh' one answers 'Blessed is He and blessed is His Name'; at 'Barukh' one answers amen (Rav Pappa). Mareimar told the Sages that their obligation of Grace was fulfilled but zimmun was lost — אֵין זִימּוּן לְמַפְרֵעַ.
